assumptions.salary_basis: net_monthly_lu = Eurostat earn_nt_net, single person without children, 100 % of the average wage, 2025, divided by 12
assumptions.commute_hours_per_month: 2 x morning minutes x 220 days / 12 / 60 (not converted into euros)
assumptions.fuel_cost_formula: 2 x road km (ChatHome, to the chosen hub) x working days / 12 x consumption / 100 x pump price; only fuel (no wear, parking, tolls or depreciation)
assumptions.left_formula: left to live (rent) = net LU reference - rent - fuel cost; null when the place has no car route
assumptions.transit_note: public transport is free in Luxembourg; cross-border train/bus fares are paid but not collected, so not counted
assumptions.rent_size_note: no open rent-by-surface-class series (only sale prices have one): no size correction applied; Luxembourg advertised flats average about 42.4 m2 (rent / rent per m2, communes with 30+ ads, weighted by ads), French ANIL values are for a 52 m2 reference flat
assumptions.dist_lux_km: straight-line distance to Luxembourg City (49.6116 N, 6.1319 E), all places
limits: Advertised rents are not rents paid; French rents are charges included (52 m2 reference apartment)
Third-party commute model, morning of a weekday: underestimates border queues
No sale prices in Moselle (DVF does not cover Alsace-Moselle)
No commute times and no rents for Belgium; German rents not comparable
Belgian prices are medians per sale (not per m2)
Commute cost = fuel only (monthly average pump price, 6.5 L/100 km, 220 days); cross-border transit fares, parking and car wear are not counted

Rent per m2 is multiplied by the chosen size without size correction: Luxembourg advertised flats average about 42 m2, so rents for 70 and 90 m2 may be overstated (per-m2 rent is usually lower for larger flats)
